verdict.rationale: Slack ships genuine natural-language AI features for end users — Slackbot as an 'AI agent' that answers questions, summarizes channels/threads, and lets users 'update deals just by asking Slackbot' or 'get fast answers with Claude' — showing users can already interact conversationally rather than via rigid UI clicks. However, most deeper actions (workflow automation, canvases, list management) still rely on no-code Workflow Builder or the MCP server aimed at external AI clients/agents rather than the human user issuing free-form NL commands for arbitrary actions. Missing for 10: evidence of broad NL-driven action execution (e.g., creating workflows, managing files/canvases) directly by a human user's natural-language command, and independent/hands-on confirmation of Slackbot's command scope beyond marketing copy.
